what_its_for: Sertaconazole nitrate is an antifungal cream used to treat a common skin infection called athlete's foot (tinea pedis). It works by killing the fungus that causes the infection, helping to relieve itching, burning, scaling, and redness between the toes and on the soles of your feet.
how_to_take: This medicine is for use on the skin only. Do not get it in your eyes, mouth, nose, or vagina. Wash and dry the affected area thoroughly before applying. Use clean hands or a cotton swab to apply a thin layer of cream to the infected skin and about 1 inch of the surrounding area. Wash your hands after applying unless your hands are the area being treated. Do not cover the treated area with tight bandages or wrappings unless your doctor tells you to.
dosing: Apply the cream to the affected area twice a day, once in the morning and once in the evening, for 4 weeks. Use it exactly as directed by your doctor, even if your symptoms improve before the 4 weeks are up. Stopping too soon may allow the fungus to come back.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, apply it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not apply a double dose to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store the cream at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep the tube tightly closed when not in use. Keep this medication out of reach of children and pets. Do not freeze the cream. Throw away any unused cream after your treatment is finished.
what_to_avoid: Avoid getting this cream in your eyes, mouth, or nose. If accidental contact occurs, rinse thoroughly with water. Do not use this cream on children under 12 years old unless directed by a doctor. Avoid wearing tight, non-breathable shoes and socks, as moisture can make the infection worse. Change your socks daily and dry your feet completely, especially between the toes, after bathing or swimming.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you notice any of the following: severe redness, burning, stinging, swelling, or blistering at the application site that was not there before; signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, hives, itching, swelling of the face or throat, difficulty breathing, or dizziness; your infection gets worse or does not improve after 2 weeks of treatment; or the infection comes back shortly after finishing your treatment.
when_it_works: You may begin to notice some improvement in your symptoms, such as less itching and redness, within the first 1 to 2 weeks of treatment. However, it is very important to continue using the cream for the full 4 weeks even if you feel better. Stopping early can cause the infection to return.
special_populations: Pregnant or breastfeeding women should talk to their doctor before using this cream. The safety of this medication in children under 12 years old has not been established, so consult your doctor before using it in young children. Elderly patients can generally use this cream safely, but should follow the same instructions as other adults.
